_comment: Drives scripts/build_surfaces.py. The NEUTRAL files are canonical and are never
written by the build; campaign surfaces are generated from them plus the variants
listed here. Adding a variant means adding an entry here, not editing the script.

fact_exceptions.September 7: Dateline. The reporting statement was rewritten 2026-09-07.
fact_exceptions.June 2: Dateline. The campaign statement is the original of 2026-06-02.
fact_exceptions.730: FM 730, a road name in the reporting statement's scope paragraph. Not a quantity.
fact_exceptions.18: '18 PDFs of tax notices', an example in the campaign statement's AI disclosure. Same 18 parcels the deck carries on both surfaces.
fact_exceptions.75: '75-megawatt' in the campaign statement's pull-quote. The deck labels that figure as testimony on both surfaces; the reporting statement does not repeat it.
fact_exceptions.1880: Typewriters, in the analogy about objections to new tools. Not a project figure.
fact_exceptions.1995: The World Wide Web, same analogy.

_exceptions_doc: Figures allowed to appear in one surface and not the other. Every entry needs a
reason, and the reason has to be that the figure is rhetorical or incidental -
never that the two surfaces disagree about the project. If a PROJECT figure ever
needs an exception, the right fix is to correct a surface, not to add an entry.
The deck carries none, and should not acquire any.
_shared_blocks_doc: A shared block is content that MUST be identical on both surfaces because it is
a matter of record rather than of voice - the corrections log above all. The
fragment is injected into the campaign output at <!-- SHARED:<name> --> and the
check asserts the same text is present in the neutral source, so neither copy
